result.rationale: The diff adds a new blocking token-refresh fetch in the SalesforceCalendarService constructor path that throws `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` before creating the jsforce connection. Previously (pre-diff code) the service constructed the connection using the existing credential; now any upstream refresh failure (rate limit, revoked token, missing app keys via getAppKeysFromSlug) throws in the constructor and breaks all Salesforce operations, even when a cached valid access_token existed. The mechanism is directly verifiable in the new code adde

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor now unconditionally performs a refresh-token fetch to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and throws `HttpError` when `response.statusText !== "OK"` (e.g., rate limits, revoked token, missing/invalid keys). There is no fallback path to proceed using the existing `credential.key` access token when refresh fails, so a transient refresh failure will prevent creating the `jsforce.Connection` and break operations that could have continued with the cached token.
